title: PoV Quick-Approval Matrix and Conditional Discount Runbook
creator: Asha M. Patel
description:
Background: Sales and Solutions Engineering teams frequently request expedited discount approvals for short-term Proof-of-Value (PoV) and channel-introduced deals. Current approval paths are slow for low-risk, high-velocity PoVs and create friction for adoption. This ticket defines a formal quick-approval matrix (monetary and contractual gates), a conditional discount runbook that ties approval paths to security questionnaire and product entitlements, and rollout tooling (templated approvals + telemetry) to make decisions auditable and reversible.

Goals: 1) Create a simple, rule-driven approval matrix for PoV deals and channel-led pilots that reduces decision time from days to hours for eligible requests. 2) Limit financial and security exposure through conditional discounts and contract templates that revert to standard terms after the PoV. 3) Integrate security questionnaire and Legal gating for entitlements that require Private deployment, KMS, or extended retention. 4) Instrument telemetry to measure adoption, downgrade/regression rate, and revenue conversion post-PoV.

Scope: - Applies to PoV deals <= $75k ARR equivalent and term <= 90 days. - Channel-led PoV deals need channel partner confirmation and standard partner addendum. - Excludes deals requiring private networking, on-prem installs, or custom compliance (those go to full Legal & Security review).

Key rules (proposed): - Tier A (auto-approve): Discounts <= 15% and net-first-year ARR <= $25k; approved by AE + SE; no Legal or Security review required. - Tier B (expedited): Discounts between 16-30% and net-first-year ARR <= $75k; requires AE + Solution Architect sign-off + Finance review; Legal passive notification; Security questionnaire auto-check for entitlements. - Tier C (full review): Discounts >30% or ARR > $75k or any requests that involve Private deployment/KMS/SSO/SOC2 deviations; routed to Legal & Security and follow standard approval ladder.

Security gating: If checkbox "requires private deployment or KMS/HSM" is selected in the PoV form, the request is escalated to Security before any discount approval. The runbook must include a short checklist for Security to perform a rapid (48 hour) triage for common ask patterns (VPC peering, KMS integration, on-prem connector).

Financial guardrails: - Maximum single PoV discount cap: 40% (requires director-level approval). - Total lifetime credits or discounts per customer via PoV program cannot exceed $100k without VP Sales approval. - All PoV discounts must auto-expire after term and revert to standard published price or negotiated renewal terms.

Operational deliverables: 1) PoV request form template (CRM/HubSpot + internal approval fields). 2) Approval matrix doc + flowchart in Confluence. 3) Slack approval shortcut (approve/deny/comment) with audit log. 4) Finance & Billing automation: apply temporary discount code that expires at PoV end. 5) Telemetry dashboard (conversion, time-to-approve, discount leakage).

Acceptance criteria: - A Confluence runbook with matrix and decision flow published and linkable from CRM. - CRM request template implemented with required gating fields. - A short Security triage checklist documented and agreed with Security team. - Finance can apply expiring discount codes via billing portal with automated expiry. - Telemetry dashboard shows time-to-approval and PoV-to-paid conversion for pilot customers.

Risks & trade-offs: - Lowering friction increases risk of discount leakage and precedent-setting; mitigated by tight caps, expiry automation, and post-PoV review. - Auto-approvals may miss subtle security needs; mitigated by mandatory checkbox gating and a 48-hour security triage. - Additional operational complexity: initial engineering/ops work for automation (billing codes, Slack integration) required; estimate 3 sprint points.

Rollout plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): publish runbook, implement CRM template, manual Slack/Email approvals. Phase 2 (4 weeks): implement automation for expiring discount codes and Slack shortcuts; collect telemetry. Phase 3 (quarterly review): evaluate metrics, adjust caps and thresholds.

References & links: - Example PoV form draft (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRG/pages/PoV-Form-Draft - Prior approval ladder doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRG/pages/Approval-Ladder - Billing API PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/488
